title: Mouse Liver Single-Cell Dissociation with Cold Protease
author: Sanjay Subramanian
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhpcj5iw

steps.title: Prepare Portal Vein for Cannulation
steps.instruction: Expose the portal vein and prepare the perfusion system.

substeps.instruction: Open the abdominal cavity and locate the main trunk of the portal vein.
Make a small incision to allow for insertion of the angled tip of the cannulation apparatus without cutting all the way through the portal vein.
Make an incision in the inferior vena cava to allow blood and perfusing solutions to flow out.
Fill a syringe with 1x PBS and attach it to the needle with the cannulation apparatus; flick the syringe and push the plunger to ensure the tubing is filled and free of air bubbles.

steps.title: Flush Liver Tissue
steps.instruction: Cannulate the portal vein and flush the liver to clear blood.

substeps.instruction: Cannulate the portal vein.
Flush 3-5 mL of ice-cold 1x PBS through the portal vein until the liver tissue is sufficiently cleared of blood.

steps.title: Perfuse Liver with Enzyme Mix
steps.instruction: Perfuse the liver with Bacillus licheniformis mixture.

substeps.instruction: Replace the PBS syringe with one containing 1 mg/mL Bacillus licheniformis mixture while keeping the portal vein cannulated.
Ensure no bubbles are in the system.
Perfuse 3-5 mL of ice-cold 1 mg/mL Bacillus licheniformis mixture through the portal vein.

steps.title: Mince and Incubate Tissue
steps.instruction: Mince the liver tissue and incubate with enzyme mix at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissect out the desired liver tissue.
Mince the tissue thoroughly with a razor blade in a petri dish containing an additional 1 mL of ice-cold Bacillus licheniformis mix.
Transfer the tissue-enzyme slurry to a 5 mL capped tube.
Incubate, rotate, or rock the tube at 4 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Secondary Mincing and Initial Filtration
steps.instruction: Further dissociate the slurry and perform initial filtration.

substeps.instruction: Mince the slurry again with a razor blade, separating or scraping larger chunks to maximize cell release.
Pass the slurry through a 100 μM filter into a 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Stop Enzyme Activity
steps.instruction: Wash cells to stop enzyme activity and increase volume.

substeps.instruction: Slowly pass ice-cold Williams' E media with 20% FBS through the filter to dislodge sticking cells and stop enzyme activity, bringing the total volume in the tube up to 10 mL.
Centrifuge cells at 250g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL Williams' E with 10% FBS.

steps.title: Secondary Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension for further purification.

substeps.instruction: Filter the suspension through a 70 μM filter into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the filter with an additional 5 mL of Williams' E 10% FBS media.

steps.title: Repeat Centrifugation and Resuspension
steps.instruction: Repeat the washing and concentration process.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 250g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL Williams' E 10% FBS (adjust final resuspension volume based on pellet size).

steps.title: Analyze and Adjust Cell Concentration
steps.instruction: Verify cell viability and adjust concentration for downstream applications.

substeps.instruction: Analyze cell morphology using a hemocytometer and Trypan blue (note: viable hepatocytes may take up trace amounts of Trypan blue).
Adjust cell concentration as needed (e.g., 700-1200 cells/μL for 10x Chromium system, target 1000 cells/μL).
